analysis.analysis: The weakest capture in the battery, and the failure is specific. Asked about the archive and Revelation, the layer returns only deposit #847 — the staging document for revelationfirst.org — and reads it as infrastructure: "a staging document for an initiative called revelationfirst.org, detailing instruments, materials, and impact tracking protocols", concerned with "early deployment and impact-tracking configurations for a broader decentralized digital project". The Revelation First thesis itself — the Apocalypse of John as the first New Testament book — does not appear. Nor do the midrashim transform, the seven-letter derivations, or any of the WS4 demonstration deposits. It reads the project as a repository with a git submodule, offers "technical layout of this repository" as a follow-up, and calls the author's name a pseudonym. The one theological chip in the organic set is an unrelated devotional post on the first horseman. Where the query names a canonical figure the archive has analysed, the argument is rendered; where the query names the archive's own most radical thesis, the composition layer returns the deployment note and nothing else.

analysis.reading:
THE ARCHIVE AS BUILD DEPENDENCY. Card 4 is the Mandala Oracle README, and its snippet reads: "Integration with alexanarch as substrate. This repository includes ALEXANARCH AS A GIT SUBMODULE." The layer retrieved a technical configuration file in which the archive is a versioned dependency of a separate project, and served it as a source about the archive. Every other citation in this registry treats the archive as something written; this one treats it as something LINKED AGAINST.

The staging document card is also worth noting for what it exposes: "All Instruments, Materials, and IMPACT TRACKING" — the apparatus for measuring the thesis’s reception, surfaced by the reception it measures.

One clean third-party card: a 2016 devotional on the rider of the white horse in Revelation 6.
